title: Canonical quotient reconstruction in the actual completed coefficient presentation
statement: Let T be any scheme and d an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Suppose the derived category of module sheaves over its actual completed coefficient sheaf has countable products. Every intrinsically complete object K [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] is a derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] of the sequence whose nth object is the restriction of K tensor^L R_n along the completed projection to R_n. The adjacent map is the restriction of the normalized quotient transition, followed by the canonical composition comparison for restrictions. No constructibility, boundedness, flatness or truncation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Final assertion: every derived I-complete object is the derived limit of its canonical strict quotient tower; transported through the actual completed-ring and finite-ring comparisons.

proof.text: Transport the supplied intrinsic-completeness certificate through the exact completed-coefficient equivalence and the descended intrinsic-completion unit. Use completedKoszulQuotientComparison to identify this intrinsic completion with completedRlim of the strict quotient tower. The invertible unit and completedRlim_roos give a distinguished Roos triangle whose first vertex is K.

Use completedReductionEvaluation at each level to identify the derived strict tower evaluations with extension followed by restriction along the actual quotient projections. Check the adjacent square on K-flat representatives using the normalization of these evaluation comparisons by the tower and scalar-extension counits. The scalar adjunction unit computes the quotient transition on pure tensors; uniqueness of maps from the sheafified tensor identifies it with the ordinary strict-tower transition. The exact restriction factorization maps identify these formulas after localization. K-flat resolutions extend the equality of natural transformations to every derived object.

The product of the level comparison isomorphisms conjugates the transition endomorphisms. Transport the two product vertices of the strict Roos triangle by this product isomorphism, retaining K as first vertex. The result is precisely the displayed IsDerivedLimit statement. No additional assumptions on the ideal, generators or scheme were used.

proof_origin.place: Canonical quotient reconstruction using the existing Koszul quotient comparison, strict Roos triangle and normalized evaluation comparisons; P8.

lean.statement:
theorem pbc_actual_completed_reduction_reconstruction
    [HasCountableProducts (PbcCompletedDerived T d)]
    (K : PbcCompletedDerived T d) (hK : PbcIsIntrinsicallyComplete T d K) :
    let M : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ PbcCompletedDerived T d :=
    Functor.ofOpSequence
        (X := fun n ↦ (pbcDerivedRestrict (pbcAdicProjection T d n)).obj
          ((pbcCompletedReduction T d n).obj K))
        (fun n ↦ (pbcDerivedRestrict (pbcAdicProjection T d (n + 1))).map
          (pbcReductionTransition (pbcAdicProjection T d (n + 1))
            (pbcAdicQuotient T d (n + 1) n (Nat.le_succ n)) (pbcAdicProjection T d n)
            (pbcAdicProjection_comp T d (n + 1) n (Nat.le_succ n)) K) ≫
          (pbcDerivedRestrictComp (pbcAdicProjection T d (n + 1))
            (pbcAdicQuotient T d (n + 1) n (Nat.le_succ n)) (pbcAdicProjection T d n)
            (pbcAdicProjection_comp T d (n + 1) n (Nat.le_succ n))).hom.app
              ((pbcCompletedReduction T d n).obj K))
    IsDerivedLimit
      (K := fun n ↦ M.obj (op n))
      (fun n ↦ M.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) K
